subcategory: India's Largest Monastery & Second Largest in the World (10,000 Ft)
description: Founded in 1680-1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso, perched like a fortress at 10,000 feet (3,048 m) in the Eastern Himalayas, India's largest Buddhist monastery and the second largest in the world after the Potala Palace in Lhasa.
why_visit: Stand in the grand three-storey Dukhang prayer hall before an 18-foot gilded Buddha statue, explore the 400-year-old library preserving ancient gold-inked Buddhist manuscripts, and witness the colorful Torgya mask dance festival.
best_time_to_visit: March to May, September to November (7:00 AM - 6:00 PM)
activities: Tibetan Buddhist Monastic Tour; Ancient Manuscript Viewing; Torgya Festival Dancing; Himalayan Photography
notes: Inner Line Permit (ILP) required for Indian domestic travelers; Protected Area Permit (PAP) for foreigners.
